The FIA may request F1 Teams to demonstrate that the specification of all relevant parts of the fuel tank, and the strength of the surrounding structure, are consistent with the pressure that the pressure relief valve is set to.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.1 Fuel tanks > C6.1.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.1 Fuel tanks > C6.1.5]
**C6.1.5** The maximum internal pressure exerted on the fuel bladder must not exceed 1.0 barG.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.1 Fuel tanks > C6.1.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2]
**C6.2** ##  Fittings and piping

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.1]
**C6.2.1** The total area of apertures in the fuel bladder must not exceed 35 000mm<sup>2</sup>.

Circular apertures smaller than 35mm diameter may be closed with a fitting, secured with a single threaded fastener on the full diameter of the opening, provided that this threaded fastener is provided with mechanical secondary locking.

All other apertures in the fuel bladder must be closed by hatches or fittings which must:

i. Be secured to metallic bolt rings bonded to the inside of the bladder.

ii. Have bolt hole edges no less than 5mm from the edge of the bolt ring, hatch, or fitting.

iii. Attach directly to the fuel bladder and have no part of the Survival Cell structure included in the closure.

iv. Be secured with multiple fasteners in such a way that the absence of any single fastener does not compromise the security of the closure.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.2]
**C6.2.2** Where the fuel bladder is attached to the Survival Cell, fixings must be designed so that if it is pulled away from the Survival Cell, the attachment will fail without compromising the integrity of the fuel bladder. For this assessment, the pull-out load for any fitting will be calculated from the clamp area between the fitting and the bladder (on one face of the bladder). Between a clamp area of 1650mm² and 9 500mm², the load will be a linear interpolation between points (1650mm², 11kN) and (9 500mm², 37.5kN). Below a clamp area of 1650mm², the load will be taken as 11kN. Above a clamp area of 9 500mm², the load will be taken as 37.5kN. No fitting may have a clamp area of less than 600 mm².

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.3]
**C6.2.3** All fuel lines between the fuel tank and the engine must have a self-sealing breakaway valve. This valve must separate at less than 50% of the load required to break the fuel line fitting or to pull it out of the fuel tank.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.4]
**C6.2.4** No lines containing fuel may pass through the Cockpit.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.5]
**C6.2.5** All lines must be fitted in such a way that any leakage cannot result in the accumulation of fuel in the Cockpit.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.6]
**C6.2.6** All components containing fuel at a pressure greater than 10barG must be located outside the fuel tank.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.2 Fittings and piping > C6.2.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.3 Fuel tank fillers > C6.3]
**C6.3** #  Fuel tank fillers

Fuel tank fillers must not protrude beyond the bodywork. Any breather pipe connecting the fuel tank to the atmosphere must be designed to avoid liquid leakage when the car is running, and its outlet must not be less than 250mm from the Cockpit opening.

All fuel tank fillers and breathers must be designed to ensure an efficient locking action which reduces the risk of an accidental opening following a crash impact or incomplete locking after refuelling.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.3 Fuel tank fillers > C6.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4]
**C6.4** #  Refuelling

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.1]
**C6.4.1** A cover must be fitted over any refuelling connector at all times when the car is running on the track. The cover and its attachments must be sufficiently strong to avoid accidental opening in the event of an accident.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.2]
**C6.4.2** The fuel in a car must not be colder than the lower of: ten degrees centigrade below ambient temperature, or ten degrees centigrade, at any time when the car is running after leaving the F1 Team's designated garage area.

The fuel in any rig used to fill the car must not be hotter than the greater of: ten degrees centigrade above ambient temperature, or thirty-five degrees centigrade, at any time.

When assessing compliance:

a. The ambient temperature will be that recorded by the FIA appointed weather service provider one hour before any practice session or three hours before the Race or Sprint Session. and will be displayed on the timing monitors.

b. The temperature of the fuel (TFFMFuel) will be that recorded in the car by the Fuel Flow Meter.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.2

page_content: [Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.3] **C6.4.3** The use of any device on board the car to decrease the temperature of the fuel is forbidden. Any system or component that increases the temperature of the fuel by means not inherent to, or exceeding, those arising from the normal operation of the car is prohibited.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.4]
**C6.4.4** Fuel may not be added to nor removed from a car during a Race.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.5]
**C6.4.5** Any refuelling procedure must respect the provisions of Article B.1.6.9.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.4 Refuelling > C6.4.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5]
**C6.5** Fuel draining and sampling

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.1]
**C6.5.1** F1 Teams must provide a means of removing all fuel from the car.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.2]
**C6.5.2** F1 Teams must ensure that a 0.70 litre sample of fuel may be taken from the car at any time during the Competition.

After a practice session, if a car has not been driven back to the pits under its own power, it will be required to supply the above-mentioned sample plus the amount of fuel that would have been consumed to drive back to the pits. The additional amount of fuel will be determined by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.3]
**C6.5.3** It must be possible to take a fuel sample drawn from the fuel collector are as defined in the fuel system hydraulic schematic shown in Article C6.6.4. To facilitate fuel sampling the car must be equipped with a - Parker Stratoflex Slide-Lok -2 Nipple or the F1 Team must provide a suitable adaptor to connect an alternative fitting to this format. If an electric pump on board the car cannot be used to remove the fuel an externally connected one may be used provided it is evident that a representative fuel sample is being taken. If an external pump is used it must be possible to connect the FIA sampling hose to it and any hose between the car and pump must be -3 in diameter and not exceed 2m in length. Details of the fuel sampling hose may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-056</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.4]
**C6.5.4** The sampling procedure must not necessitate starting the engine or the removal of bodywork (other than the nosebox assembly and the cover over any refuelling connector).

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.5 Fuel draining and sampling > C6.5.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6]
**C6.6** Fuel System Hydraulic Layout

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.1]
**C6.6.1** Parts listed in Appendix C6 sections 6A and 6E are classified as OSC.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.2]
**C6.6.2** The primer pump(s) and Fuel Flow Meter are SSC, the High Pressure Fuel Pump and the pressure and temperature sensors are SSPUC; as mandated by the FIA and specified in the following documents <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-003</mark>, <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-017</mark>, <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-018</mark> and <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-019</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.3]
**C6.6.3** All flexible pipes and hoses and their fittings between the primer pump and the High Pressure Fuel Pump are SSC, as mandated by the FIA. The specification and permitted lengths are given in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-013</mark>. Rigid pipes and manifolds and their fittings may be used instead of flexible pipes and hoses up to the inlet of the Fuel Flow Meter. Rigid pipes and manifolds may also be used at the Fuel Flow Meter outlet but only for connection to the optional filter or to support the pressure and temperature sensor. Such rigid pipes and manifolds are classified as OSC.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.4] **C6.6.4** The hydraulic layout of the fuel system must functionally conform to the schematic given in the drawing below. Additional components (such as collector pressurisation system) are permitted, subject to the approval of the FIA if they are deemed necessary for the proper behaviour of the system. metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.5]
**C6.6.5** If a fuel pressure damper is fitted it must be fitted upstream of the Fuel Flow Meter described in article C5.9.3.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.6]
**C6.6.6** The pressure of the fuel inside the collector may be increased relative to the pressure in the fuel cell volume by the lift pumps and/or either

i. air pressure acting on the free surface of the fuel,

ii. or hydraulic oil or air pressure acting on a piston.

In all cases the increase in pressure in the collector must be for the sole purpose of maintaining the primer pump(s) inlet pressure above the cavitation point. And it must be demonstrated to the

satisfaction of the FIA that any fluid used for this purpose cannot be used to change the composition of the fuel.

*Advisory Committee: TAC*
*Governance: F1 Commission / WMSC*

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C6: FUEL SYSTEM > C6.6 Fuel System Hydraulic Layout > C6.6.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.1 Location of lubricating oil tanks > C7.1]
**C7.1** ##  Location of lubricating oil tanks

All oil storage tanks must be situated between X<sub>F</sub>=0 and X<sub>DIF</sub>=150, and must be no further outboard than the lateral extremities of the Survival Cell.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.1 Location of lubricating oil tanks > C7.1
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING
metadata.sub_article: C7.1 Location of lubricating oil tanks

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.2 Location of lubricating oil system > C7.2]
**C7.2** ##  Location of lubricating oil system

No other part of the car containing lubricating oil may be situated behind X<sub>DIF</sub> = 150 or outboard of Y=750.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.2 Location of lubricating oil system > C7.2
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING
metadata.sub_article: C7.2 Location of lubricating oil system

[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3]
**C7.3** ##  Oil and coolant lines

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3.1]
**C7.3.1** No lines containing coolant or lubricating oil may pass through the Cockpit.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3.1
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3.2]
**C7.3.2** All lines must be fitted in such a way that any leakage cannot result in the accumulation of fluid in the Cockpit.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3.2

[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.3 Oil and coolant lines > C7.3.3]
**C7.3.3** No hydraulic fluid lines may have removable connectors inside the cockpit.

[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.4 Heat exchangers > C7.4]
**C7.4** ##  Heat exchangers

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.4 Heat exchangers > C7.4
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.4 Heat exchangers > C7.4.1]
**C7.4.1** ###  Primary heat exchanger specification and technology

For Primary Heat Exchangers used on the car, the following restrictions apply:

a. The Heat Exchanger Core and header tanks must be made from aluminium alloy.

b. The Heat Exchanger Core must not be produced using additive manufacturing.

c. Heat Exchanger Tubes must have a wall thickness of at least 0.18mm.

d. The internal cross section of any Heat Exchanger Tube must have an area of at least 10mm², without considering structural stiffening ribs and the internal fins described in point (e) below.

e. Heat Exchanger Fins fitted inside the tubes must have a thickness of at least 0.06mm. Heat Exchanger Fins fitted between the tubes must have a minimum thickness of 0.05mm.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.4 Heat exchangers > C7.4.1
metadata.article: Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING

page_content:
[Section C > Article C7: OIL AND COOLANT SYSTEMS AND CHARGE AIR COOLING > C7.4 Heat exchangers > C7.4.2]
**C7.4.2** ###  Secondary heat exchanger specification and technology

Secondary Heat Exchangers must be constructed from metallic materials with the exception of any sealing or bonding.

*Advisory Committee: TAC*
*Governance: F1 Commission / WMSC*

[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1]
**C8.1** ##  Software and electronics inspection

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.1]
**C8.1.1** Prior to the start of each season the complete electrical and electronic system on the car must be examined and all on board and communications hardware and software must be inspected by the FIA Technical Department.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.2]
**C8.1.2** The FIA must be notified of any changes prior to the Competition at which such changes are intended to be implemented.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.3]
**C8.1.3** All re-programmable devices must have a mechanism that allows the FIA to accurately identify the software version loaded.

Acceptable solutions to verify the programmed software may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-033</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.4]
**C8.1.4** All electronic units containing a programmable device, and which are intended for use at a Competition, must be presented to the FIA before each Competition in order that they can be identified.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.5]
**C8.1.5** All on-car software versions must be registered with the FIA before use.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.6]
**C8.1.6** The FIA must be able to test the operation of any compulsory electronic safety systems at any time during a Competition.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.7]
**C8.1.7** F1 Teams may only run custom software that has been homologated by the FIA for their control applications hosted inside or outside the ECU described in Article C8.1.1.

Details of the homologation process can be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-033</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.7

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.8]
**C8.1.8** The number of versions used in any single championship season will be limited as shown in the table below. Figures are given per custom control application.



||2026See Note 1|2027|2028|2029|2030|
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
|ECU F1 Team applications|5|4|3|3|3|
|ECU PU applications|5|4|3|3|3|
|ERS and PU-CE Applications|5|4|3|3|3|


A version will be deemed to have been used once the car’s timing transponder has shown that it has left the pit lane.

Changes made solely for reliability, bug fix, compatibility with standard or other custom applications or changes requested by the FIA will not increase the version counter.

Note 1: for the 2026 Championship season only, the limits defined in the above table will apply starting from the fifth Competition.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.1 Software and electronics inspection > C8.1.8

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2]
**C8.2** ## **** **Control electronics

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.1]
**C8.2.1** All components of the Power Unit, fuel system, transmission systems, brake system, tyre pressure monitoring system and adjustable bodywork in addition to all associated actuators, must be controlled by the FIA Standard ECU.

The FIA Standard ECU may only be used with FIA approved software and may only be connected to the control system wiring loom, sensors and actuators in a manner specified by the FIA.

Additional information regarding the FIA Standard ECU software versions and setup may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-033</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.2]
**C8.2.2** All ECUs, control sensors, and actuators will be homologated by the FIA. In addition, non-control sensors or units connected to the FIA Standard ECU must also be homologated. Details of the homologation process may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-033</mark>.

Each and every component of the control system will be sealed and uniquely identified and their identities tracked through their life cycle.

These components and units may not be disassembled or modified in any way and seals and identifiers must remain intact and legible.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.3]
**C8.2.3** The control system wiring loom connectivity must be approved by the FIA.

All wiring looms must be built to ensure that each control sensor and each control actuator is electrically isolated from non-control sensors.

In general, there must be no active or passive electronic component in the control loom. Exceptions (e.g. termination resistors) must be approved by the FIA before use.

Additional wiring guidelines may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-033</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.4]
**C8.2.4** If sensor faults or errors are detected by the driver or by the on-board software, back-up sensors may be used and different settings may be manually or automatically selected. However, any back-up sensor or new setting chosen in this way must not enhance the performance of the car. Any driver default turned on during the start lockout period may not be turned off before the end of that period.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.5]
**C8.2.5** Pneumatic valve pressure may only be controlled via a passive mechanical regulator or from the FIA Standard ECU and its operation will be monitored by the FIA Standard ECU.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.2 Control electronics > C8.2.5

[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3]
**C8.3** ## **** **Start systems

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3.1]
**C8.3.1** Any system, the purpose and/or effect of which is to detect when a race start signal is given, is not permitted.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3.2]
**C8.3.2** The FIA Standard ECU will implement a "lockout" period after each race start or pit stop during which a number of Power Unit and transmission related functions will be frozen or disabled.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.3 Start systems > C8.3.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4]
**C8.4** ## **** **Data acquisition

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4.1]
**C8.4.1** To assist scrutineering, the FIA requires unlimited access to the following FIA Standard ECU information before, during and after any track session

a. Application parameter configurations.

b. Logged data and events.

c. Real-time Telemetry data and events.

Throughout the Competition, the logging memory and events buffer may only be cleared by an FIA engineer.

The FIA must have the ability to connect to the FIA Standard ECU via an F1 Team-provided

standalone equipment using an FIA laptop. The F1 Teams should make a jump battery available at all times during the Competition.

The F1 Teams should transfer the real-time Telemetry data and events on the FIA network as

requested by, and in the format defined by, the FIA. Prior to the Race or Sprint Session, the FIA Standard ECU data logger must be configured in such a way that allows logging of data for at least two hours and fifteen minutes without exceeding the size of the logger memory.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4.2]
**C8.4.2** Any data acquisition system, Telemetry system or associated sensors additional to those provided by the FIA Standard ECU and FIA ADR must be physically separate and electrically isolated from

any Control Electronics with the exception of:

a. The primary regulated voltage supply.

b. The car system ground.

c. Communication links to the FIA Standard ECU, Telemetry unit and FIA ADR.

d. Power supplies, provided they are not used to power any Control Electronics, control sensors or actuators.

e. Time synchronisation lines.

f. Power Unit synchronisation lines.

g. An umbilical loom whose connector will remain disconnected when the car is moving.

Unless approved by the FIA, no junction box or break-out box may be shared between the FIA

Standard ECU system and an F1 Team data acquisition system. The use of any coupling, be it hard wired, magnetic, optical or other such link which allows the

transmission of signals will not be considered as adequate isolation in the context of this Article.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.4 Data acquisition > C8.4.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5]
**C8.5** ##  Telemetry

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.1]
**C8.5.1** All cars must be fitted with a car to F1 Team Telemetry system which has been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.2]
**C8.5.2** Telemetry systems must operate at frequencies which have been approved by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.3]
**C8.5.3** F1 Team to car Telemetry is prohibited, with the exception of

a. The FIA Marshalling System defined in Article C8.11;

b. Handshaking required by the car to F1 Team telemetry system defined in Article C8.5.1.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.4]
**C8.5.4** The CCU Antenna must be mounted

a. respecting the requirements of <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>.

b. symmetrically about the plane Y = 0.

c. such that “Point X” lies:

```
i. between planes X<sub>C</sub> = 350 and X<sub>C</sub> = 750.

Ii. between planes Z = 830 and Z = 970.
```

d. such that “Surface Z” forms an angle between 0 and -20 degrees (nose up) to the plane Z = 0.

Furthermore, referring to <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>, any part of the car (except the CCU Antenna) in the residual region defined below which intersects “Zone A” must be constructed of radio transparent material approved by the FIA designated supplier of the F1 Team Telemetry system:

e. above a Z-plane coincident with the lowest point of “Surface Z”.

f. above a plane coincident with “Surface Z”.

g. behind an X-plane lying 100mm ahead of “Point X”.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.5 Telemetry > C8.5.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6]
**C8.6** #  Driver inputs and information

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.1]
**C8.6.1** With the exception of voice radio communication, all signals associated with driver information and driver input devices must be generated by the FIA Standard ECU.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.2]
**C8.6.2** Any single input device, including but not limited to switch, button, paddle or pedal, used by the driver must be connected to a single analogue or digital input of the FIA Standard ECU.

Exceptions will be considered to handle the following:

a. A spare clutch paddle sensor.

b. A spare accelerator pedal sensor.

c. A separate "kick−down" sensor which indicates that the accelerator pedal has been deliberately depressed past full travel.

d. Multiplexed shift signals.

e. A spare brake pressure and pedal sensor.

Any interface between such driver input devices and the FIA Standard ECU must be approved by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.3]
**C8.6.3** Any alteration of the driver’s inputs may only be commanded by direct, deliberate and primary driver actions.

The logged raw signals from the FIA Standard ECU inputs must provide a true representation of the driver’s actions.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.4]
**C8.6.4** #  Accelerator Pedal

The only means by which the driver may control acceleration torque to the driven wheels is via a single foot (accelerator) pedal mounted inside the Survival Cell.

The design or installation of any component, surface finish, or feature, the purpose or effect of which allow specific points between the 0% and 100% calibrated references of the accelerator

pedal travel range to be identified by the driver or to assist the driver to hold a position are not permitted.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.6 Driver inputs and information > C8.6.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7]
**C8.7** ##  Master switch

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7.1]
**C8.7.1** The driver, when seated normally with the safety belts fastened and the steering wheel in place, must be able to cut off the electrical circuits to the ignition, all fuel pumps and the rear lights by means of a spark proof circuit breaker switch.

This switch must be located on the dashboard and must be clearly marked by a symbol showing a red spark in a white edged blue triangle.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7.2]
**C8.7.2** There must also be two exterior horizontal handles which are capable of being operated from a distance by a hook. These handles must be situated at the base of the main roll over structure on both sides of the car and have the same function as the switch described in Article C8.7.1.

The handles must enclose a circle of diameter 40mm and be red or yellow if the surrounding bodywork is predominantly red.

The handles must be marked with a letter "E" in red at least 80mm tall, with a line thickness of at least 8mm, inside a white disc of at least 100mm diameter with a red edge with a line thickness of at least 4mm.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.7 Master switch > C8.7.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8]
**C8.8** ##  Driver radio

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8.1]
**C8.8.1** All cars must be fitted with a voice radio communication system which has been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8.2]
**C8.8.2** Other than authorised connections to the FIA Standard ECU, any voice radio communication system between car and pits must be stand alone and must not transmit or receive other data. All such communications must be open and accessible to both the FIA and broadcasters.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.8 Driver radio > C8.8.2
Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.1]
**C8.9.1** ##  FIA ADR

The FIA ADR must be fitted and operated:

a. In accordance with the instructions of the FIA.

b. With its centre plane no more than 25mm from Y=0 and with its top facing upwards.

c. With each of its 12 edges parallel to the coordinate system defined in Article C2.1.

d. In a position within the Cockpit which is readily accessible at all times from within the Cockpit without the need to remove plank or floor.

e. Positioned so that the entire unit lies:

either

i. Behind RV−COCKPIT−DRIVER, between X<sub>C</sub> = −475and X<sub>C</sub> = 100 and below Z=440, with its connectors facing forward,

or

ii. Ahead of RV−COCKPIT−DRIVER, behind X<sub>C</sub> = −1075 and below Z=250, with its connectors facing either forward or rearward.

f. Via anti−vibration mountings giving a clearance of 5mm to all other objects.

g. In order that the download connector is easily accessible when the driver is seated normally and without the need to remove bodywork.

h. Within the operating limits specified by the supplier, in particular the maximum temperature limits.

The FIA ADR must be powered from a nominally 12V supply such that its internal battery can be recharged at all times when the car’s electronic systems are powered and when the car systems are switched off, but a jump battery or umbilical is connected.

Details of the connections to the FIA ADR may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-038</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.2]
**C8.9.2** #  External accelerometer

The FIA ADR must be connected to one external 500g accelerometer which has been manufactured by a FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

The accelerometer must be fitted:

a. In accordance with the instructions of the FIA.

b. Within the Cockpit, solidly bolted to the Survival Cell using four 4mm bolts, with a body clearance of 5mm to all other objects.

c. With each of its 12 edges parallel to and matching the coordinate system defined in Article C2.1.

d. In order that the entire accelerometer body lies as close as possible to the plane Y=0 and within an axis−aligned cube with an internal diagonal bounded by points \[X<sub>C</sub>, Y, Z] \[−500, −130, 0] and \[−250, 130, 150].

e. In a position which is readily accessible at all times from within the Cockpit when the seat is removed.

Details of the accelerometer may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-028</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.3]
**C8.9.3** #  High speed camera

Each car must be fitted with a high speed camera which has been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

The camera must be fitted in accordance with the instructions of the FIA, details of which may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-029</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.4]
**C8.9.4** #  In−ear accelerometers

Each driver must wear in−ear accelerometers which have been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.5]
**C8.9.5** #  Biometric device

For the purpose of aiding driver rescue, the FIA may define biometric devices, to be worn by each driver and which have been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.9 Accident analysis > C8.9.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.10 Accident data > C8.10]
**C8.10** #  Accident data

At any time following an accident or incident F1 Teams must make the FIA ADR available and accessible to the FIA. A representative of the F1 Team concerned may be present when data relevant to an accident or incident is being uploaded from the recorder. A copy of the data will be made available to the F1 Team.

Any conclusions as to the cause of an accident, or any data relevant to an accident, may only be published in the form of a report which has been agreed between the F1 Team concerned and the FIA.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.10 Accident data > C8.10

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.11 FIA Marshalling system > C8.11]
**C8.11** #  FIA Marshalling system

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.11 FIA Marshalling system > C8.11

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.11 FIA Marshalling system > C8.11.1]
**C8.11.1** ##  All cars must be fitted with a marshalling system, comprising a car positioning system and a bidirectional race control to car communication system, which has been manufactured by the FIA designated supplier to a specification determined by the FIA.

No other parts which, in the opinion of the FIA are capable of performing a similar function, may be fitted to any car.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.11 FIA Marshalling system > C8.11.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.11 FIA Marshalling system > C8.11.2]
**C8.11.2** ##  Car Positioning Unit

The Car Positioning Unit must be positioned in the forward part of the Survival Cell respecting the requirements of <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-023</mark>.

[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.12 Track signal information display > C8.12]
**C8.12** #  Track signal information display

All cars must be fitted with red, blue and yellow Cockpit lights, supplied as part of the FIA Standard ECU, the purpose of which are to give drivers information concerning track signals or conditions. The lights must be fitted directly in the driver’s normal line of sight.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.12 Track signal information display > C8.12

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.13 Impact warning system > C8.13]
**C8.13** ##  Impact warning system

In order to give rescue crews an immediate indication of accident severity each car must be fitted with a warning light which is connected to the FIA ADR.

The light must face upwards and be recessed into the top of the Survival Cell and be positioned according to Drawing 10 of Appendix C3.

Details of the light and its control system may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-031</mark>.

**C8.14** ##  Installation of electrical systems or components

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.14 Installation of electrical systems or components > C8.14
metadata.sub_article: C8.14 Installation of electrical systems or components

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.14 Installation of electrical systems or components > C8.14.1]
**C8.14.1** Exceptionally, each car may be equipped with a maximum of five test sensor installations, which do not comply with Article C3, during P1 and P2, provided

a. They could not materially affect the outcome any of the impact tests described in Article C13.

b. They lie entirely within an axis-aligned cuboid with an internal diagonal bounded by points \[X<sub>F</sub> = -1300, -925, -200] and \[X<sub>R</sub> = 1000, 925, 1100].

c. No part of any sensor may lie above a triangular surface with vertices at \[X<sub>C</sub> = -200, 0, 655], \[X<sub>F</sub> = -1300, 1225, 655] and \[X<sub>F</sub> = -1300, -1225, 655].

d. They do not obstruct on-board camera views.

e. If attached to either the RIS or the FIS, they may only use fixings that were present at the homologation of the structure.

Any such test sensor installations do not need to be homologated.

The FIA technical delegate must be notified of any intended use of such non-C3 compliant test sensor installations prior to the Competition at which they are first used.

**C8.15** ##  Timing transponders

All cars must be fitted with two timing transponders supplied by the officially appointed timekeepers. These transponders must be fitted in strict accordance with the instructions detailed in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>. F1 Teams must use their best endeavours to ensure that the transponders are in working order at all times.

[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16]
**C8.16** ##  Cameras and camera housings

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.1]
**C8.16.1** At all times throughout the Competition, cars must be equipped with six positions in which cameras or camera housings can be fitted. Referring to Drawing 2 of Appendix C3, all cars must carry

a. a camera in positions 4, and 5.
b. a camera or camera housing in positions 1 and 2

If requested by the Commercial Rights Holder, a car must carry;

a. a camera in positions 4, and 5.

c. a camera fitted in the driver’s helmet and pointing forward,

d. a camera in position 6.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.1

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.2]
**C8.16.2** Details concerning the technical specification of all cameras may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.2

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.3]
**C8.16.3** With the exception of the position in the driver’s helmet, camera housings, when used, must be fitted in the same location as cameras, and satisfy all the relevant regulations. They must be identical in size, shape, and mass to the camera in lieu of which they are fitted, and must be supplied by the relevant F1 Team. Details concerning the shape and mass of all camera housings may be found in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>.

Any decision as to whether a camera or camera housing is fitted in those positions will be by agreement between the relevant F1 Team and the Commercial Rights Holder.

If a car is not required to carry either a camera in the helmet of the driver, or a camera in position 6, ballast of 0.35 kg must be securely fitted in the location of the Helmet Camera Processing Unit.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.3

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.4]
**C8.16.4** F1 Teams must be notified of any changes to the camera or transponder installation instructions before 30 June of the previous season.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.4

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.5]
**C8.16.5** Any camera fitted in positions 2, 3 or 4 shown in Drawing 2 of Appendix C3 must be mounted in order that its major axis does not subtend an angle greater than 1° to the plane Z=0, and its lateral axis is normal to the plane Y=0.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.5

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.6]
**C8.16.6** Position 1

Any camera fitted in position 1 must be fitted above the Survival Cell, forward of the Cockpit opening, rearwards of the forward attachment of the Secondary Roll Structure. and symmetrically with respect to the plane Y=0, with the camera pointing towards the driver. The electronic conditioning unit for this camera must be positioned within the Survival Cell and in accordance with the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.6

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.7]
**C8.16.7** Position 2

On the left-hand side, a camera, or camera housing of the same mass must be fitted.

On the right-hand side, a lightweight camera housing, or a diagnostic camera defined in Article C3.18.15 (if required by the FIA) must be fitted symmetrically to the camera on the left-hand side.

The entire camera or housing in position 2 must lie within RV−CAMERA−2.

The camera fitted in position 2 shown in Drawing 2 of Appendix C3 must be mounted in order that its major axis where passing through the centre of the camera lens does not intersect any part of the car lying forward of the camera.

Any part provided by the F1 Team for the purpose of aligning the camera or housing in position 2 correctly will be considered part of the camera provided it does not exceed 25mm in width and is being fitted for that sole purpose.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.7

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.8]
**C8.16.8** #  Position 3

The camera fitted in position 3 must be mounted in order that its forward−most point is situated between X<sub>C</sub> = 0 and X<sub>C</sub> = 300 and between <mark>Z = 840</mark> and Z = 900. The inner face of the camera should be between Y = 120 and Y = 170.

Any part provided by the Competitor for the purpose of aligning the camera in position 3 must be an extrusion of the camera unit profile. A radius of up to 10mm will be permitted where this component meets the bodywork or survival cell.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.8

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.9]
**C8.16.9** #  Position 4

The camera fitted in position 4 must be mounted in order that its forward−most point is forward of X<sub>C</sub> = 80.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.9

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.10]
**C8.16.10** #  Position 5

The camera fitted in position 5 must be mounted, symmetrically about Y=0, with the lens centre forward of X<sub>C</sub> = −1250 and with its lower surface at an angle no greater than 6° to the plane Z=0. In order to not impinge on its 360deg image, any shrouding or cutout should be no higher than “Shoulder X”, as defined in the document <mark>FIA-F1-DOC-022</mark>.

metadata.breadcrumb: Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.10

page_content:
[Section C > Article C8: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS > C8.16 Cameras and camera housings > C8.16.11]
**C8.16.11** #  Position 6

The camera fitted in position 6 must be mounted within the Rear Impact Structure with the face of the lens pointing rearwards at an angle no greater than 1° to the plane X=0.

**C8.17** #  Electromagnetic radiation

Electromagnetic radiation between 2.0 and 2.7GHz is forbidden save with the written consent of the FIA.
